name: Naturpark Kaunergrat
kurzbeschreibung: Kaunergrat Nature Park spans rugged alpine valleys, mystical peat bogs, and the striking Gachenblick visitor centre overlooking the dramatic peaks of the Ötztal Alps.
preis: Free access to trails (Naturparkhaus exhibition charges admission)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; Naturparkhaus open May to October and in winter
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Kaunergrat Nature Park encompasses all altitudinal vegetation belts of the Ötztal Alps, stretching between the Kaunertal, Pitztal, and upper Inn valleys in the Tyrolean Oberland. It ranks among the most pristine and biologically diverse nature reserves in the Central Eastern Alps. Named after the jagged granite-gneiss crest of the Kaunergrat ridge, crowned by the formidable Watzespitze (3,532 m), this park is celebrated for its extraordinary ecological contrasts. Within a short distance, sun-baked dry grassland slopes in the valleys transition into ancient stone pine woodlands, mysterious post-glacial peat bogs like the Piller Moor, and sparkling glacial tongues. Over 1,100 butterfly species, rare wild orchids, and robust herds of alpine ibex thrive in this protected alpine sanctuary.

Route & Anforderungen

Hiking trails within Kaunergrat Nature Park offer rewarding experiences tailored to every fitness level. A must-visit attraction for families and nature lovers is the barrier-free peat bog nature trail through the Piller Moor, navigating raised wooden boardwalks past carnivorous sundew plants to a scenic observation tower. For experienced mountain hikers, demanding high-altitude routes like the Kaunergrat Panorama Trail or hikes toward the Verpeilhütte refuge require surefootedness, good physical endurance, and mountain boots. A popular hub for excursions is the striking Naturparkhaus visitor centre perched on the Gachenblick ridge at 1,560 metres, boasting an awe-inspiring viewing platform cantilevered over the Inn Valley.

Besuch & Anreise

The Naturparkhaus at Piller Sattel (Gachenblick) is situated at the junction connecting the mountain communities of Fließ, Wenns, and Kauns. From Landeck or Imst, the mountain pass is reachable by car via paved roads in approximately twenty minutes, with ample parking adjacent to the centre. Public transit connections are operated by regular regional post buses departing from Landeck-Zams and Imst-Pitztal railway stations. The centre features the interactive multimedia exhibition '3,000 m Vertical' alongside a panoramic restaurant serving regional specialties.

Tipps

Be sure to tour the '3,000 m Vertical' exhibition to uncover how wildlife adapts from dry valley bottoms to icy summits. Concluding your day with a peaceful twilight walk along the boardwalks of the Piller Moor offers exceptional landscape photography opportunities amidst tranquil mountain reflections.
